podcast-dannyjones-BThnZz-ryHg:
Jesse Michels hosts a program of his own on hidden history and strange science. On Danny Jones's podcast the two compare territories. They cover UFO whistleblowers and claims of NASA time travel research. They also cover the psychic soldiers of the military's remote viewing programs.

Michels moves fluently between documented programs and rumored ones, and part of the episode's work is sorting which is which. The psychic soldier material rests on real declassified files; the time travel claims do not. Jones and Michels share sources and argue about their weight. For listeners, the conversation works as a map of the modern UFO world's main roads, drawn by two of its busiest guides. It is preserved as their map, with the borders between fact and lore left for the audience to patrol.
podcast-dannyjones-JVzyt7z7mhg:
Jeremy Rys researches the UFO phenomenon's documentary record. He joins Danny Jones to present what he calls explosive new evidence in the Bob Lazar case. He also brings Area 51 secrets he says can now be revealed. Lazar's 1989 claims about working on alien craft near Area 51 made him the whistleblower archetype, and they remain unverified and fiercely argued.

Rys works the paper trail: employment records, timing, and the statements of others placed near Lazar's story. Jones follows the documents rather than the legend. Believers will hear corroboration; skeptics will hear the same gaps as always. The episode's value is its method, a researcher laying out exhibits in order. It preserves the Lazar debate in its current state, evidence-focused and unresolved, for an audience still split by a story told the year the Berlin Wall fell.
podcast-tuckercarlson-1cbw1utqzHg:
Former Green Beret Joe Kent speaks to Tucker Carlson in his first interview since resigning as Trump's counterterrorism director. Kent, who lost his wife to a bombing in Syria, served in the role before stepping down. His exit raised questions this candid hour sets out to answer.

Kent explains why he resigned and what he saw inside the counterterrorism machine. He shares his soldier's view of the wars America keeps entering and the costs at home. Carlson asks what warnings he would give the president now. Patriotic and curious viewers get an insider account from a man who walked away.
